You are reverse-engineering, PURELY AS A BLACK BOX, the behavior of this program:

    /workspace/dataset/test5_executable --a '<instance JSON>' --b '<schema JSON>'

It is a PyInstaller bundle of this Python script (jsonschema 4.23.0, CPython 3.x):

    instance = json.loads(args.a); schema = json.loads(args.b)
    validator = Draft7Validator(schema)
    errors = list(validator.iter_errors(instance))
    print(len(errors))

So stdout is the NUMBER OF TOP-LEVEL ValidationErrors yielded by iter_errors, then a newline.
Nonzero exit = unhandled Python exception (stdout empty). Exit 2 = argparse usage error.

RULES OF ENGAGEMENT:
- NEVER run 'python'/'python3'. Only run the executable. Do not try to unpack or read the bundle's source.
- Your job is EMPIRICAL: form a hypothesis, then run cases to confirm/refute. Report only what you OBSERVED.
- The consumer of your report is an engineer reimplementing this in pure Node.js ESM with zero dependencies.
  What they need from you: exact error-count semantics, and every place naive JS would diverge from Python.

WORKFLOW (do all of it):
1. Author a case file /workspace/probe/cases/<FAMILY>.json — a JSON array of {"a": "<instance json string>", "b": "<schema json string>", "note": "what this pins down"}.
   Write it with the Write tool (it is plain JSON; remember a/b are STRINGS containing JSON).
2. Run: node /workspace/probe/harness.mjs /workspace/probe/cases/<FAMILY>.json
   It prints one line per case (out="N\n" or EXIT code) and saves observed results to /workspace/probe/observed/<FAMILY>.json.
   You may also invoke the executable directly for quick one-off checks.
3. Iterate: when a result surprises you, add cases to isolate the rule. Aim for 45-110 cases that are DECISIVE, not repetitive.
4. IMPORTANT: every case in your final case file must have been run through the harness so its observed output is recorded.
   The observed file is the regression corpus the implementer will test against - it must be complete and correct.

Report your findings via the structured output tool. Be dense and specific: "properties yields one error per failing
subschema, and nested errors propagate individually (instance {"a":{"b":1}} vs properties.a.properties.b.type=string
plus a.required=[z,y] => 3)" is useful; "properties works as expected" is useless.

You are the COMPLETENESS CRITIC for family "regex-pattern". Another agent already probed it and wrote
/workspace/probe/cases/regex-pattern.json (observed results in /workspace/probe/observed/regex-pattern.json).

Their report:
RULES:
- ENGINE: `pattern` is evaluated as Python `re.search(schema_pattern, instance)` -> UNANCHORED, and yields AT MOST 1 error. instance "abc": pattern "b"=>0, "^b"=>1, "b$"=>1, "^abc$"=>0, ""=>0.
- LAZY COMPILE: `pattern` is only touched when the instance is a JSON string. instance 123 or {"x":1} with pattern "^a$" => 0; instance 5 with the INVALID pattern "[" => 0 (no exception). Same for patternProperties on a non-object, and for a string instance carrying a bogus patternProperties: {"pattern":"b","patternProperties":{"[":{}}} vs "abc" => 0.
- NON-STRING pattern VALUE => exception: {"pattern":5} and {"pattern":null} => TypeError 'first argument must be string or compiled pattern'; {"pattern":["b"]} => TypeError 'unhashable type: list'. All exit 1, empty stdout.
- NO FLAGS are passed by jsonschema: matching is case-SENSITIVE, non-MULTILINE, non-DOTALL by default ("ABC" vs "^abc$" => 1). Flags are only obtainable via inline (?imsxau) groups at the very start of the pattern.
- $ SEMANTICS: `$` matches at end-of-string OR immediately before exactly ONE trailing \n. "a\n" vs "a$" => 0, vs "^a$" => 0; "\n" vs "^$" => 0; "a\n\n" vs "a$" => 1; "a\r" vs "a$" => 1; "a\r\n" vs "a$" => 1; interior newline not special: "a\nb" vs "a$"/"^a$"/"^b$" => 1,1,1. Trailing-\n tolerance still holds under (?m): "a\n" vs "(?m)a$" => 0.
- \Z = absolute end (no newline tolerance): "a" vs "a\\Z" => 0, "a\n" => 1, "aZ" => 1. \A = absolute start: "a" vs "\\Aa" => 0, "Aa" => 1. \z is NOT supported: pattern "a\\z" => exception (re.error: bad escape \z).
- DOT: `.` excludes ONLY \n. "^a.b$" matches "a\rb"=>0, "a b"=>0, "a b"=>0, "ab"=>0, but "a\nb" vs "a.b" => 1; "(?s)a.b" vs "a\nb" => 0.
- (?m) LINE BOUNDARY is \n ONLY. "a\nb" vs "(?m)^b$" => 0, but "a\rb" => 1, "a b" => 1, "a b" => 1. "\n" vs "(?m)^$" => 0.
- \d = Unicode category Nd. Matches: U+0663 Arabic-Indic 3 =>0, U+FF11 fullwidth 1 =>0, U+0F20 Tibetan 0 =>0. Does NOT match U+00B2 (No) =>1, U+2160 (Nl) =>1. \D is the exact complement (U+0663 vs "^\\D$" => 1). Inside a class it is identical: U+0663 vs "^[\\d]$" => 0, but "^[0-9]$" => 1.
- \w = Unicode word chars (letters of all categories + Nd/No/Nl + '_'). Matches U+0663=>0, U+00E9=>0, U+00B2=>0, U+00BD=>0, U+2160=>0, U+00B5=>0, U+4E2D=>0, U+02B0=>0, "_"=>0. Does NOT match combining marks: U+0301 alone =>1 and "é" vs "^\\w+$" =>1; emoji U+1F600 =>1; "-" =>1.
- \s = Python Unicode whitespace: matches U+00A0=>0, U+3000=>0, U+000B=>0, U+001C=>0, U+001D=>0, U+001F=>0, U+0085=>0, U+2028=>0, U+2029=>0. Does NOT match U+001B=>1, U+FEFF=>1, U+200B=>1. \S is the exact complement (U+001C vs "^\\S$"=>1, U+FEFF vs "^\\S$"=>0). Identical inside a class (U+001C vs "^[\\s]$"=>0).
- WORD BOUNDARY \b/\B are Unicode-aware because \w is: "éx" vs "\\bx" => 1 and vs "\\Bx" => 0; "٣x" vs "\\bx" => 1. ASCII baseline: "foo bar" vs "\\bbar\\b" => 0, "foobar" vs "\\bbar" => 1.
- INLINE FLAG SUPPORT: (?a) forces ASCII (U+0663 vs "(?a)^\\d$" => 1; U+00E9 vs "(?a)^\\w$" => 1). (?u) is a no-op. (?i)(?s) as two separate groups at the start is fine ("abc" vs "(?i)(?s)^A.C$" => 0) as is combined "(?is)^A.C$" => 0. (?L) with a str pattern is an exception.
- GLOBAL INLINE FLAGS MUST BE AT POSITION 0: "a(?i)b", "^(?i)abc$", "((?i)a)" all => exception (re.error: global flags not at the start of the expression); "(?i)^a(?-i)b$" => exception (missing : at position 10). SCOPED flag groups work anywhere: "aB" vs "^a(?i:b)$" => 0; "AB" vs "(?i)^a(?-i:b)$" => 1.
- CODE POINTS, NOT UTF-16 UNITS: an astral char is ONE character. "😀" vs "^.$" => 0 and vs "^..$" => 1; "a😀b" vs "^a.b$" => 0; vs "^[\\u0000-\\uffff]$" => 1. A lone surrogate survives json.loads and counts as 1 char: "\ud800" vs "^.$" => 0.
- PYTHON-ONLY SYNTAX THAT WORKS (all 0 errors when matching): (?P<n>a) ; (?P<n>a)(?P=n) vs "aa" ; (?P<n>a)\\1 vs "aa" ; (?#comment)a ; "(?x) a  b " vs "ab" ; octal \\101 vs "A" ; \\0 vs U+0000 ; \\N{LATIN SMALL LETTER A} vs "a" ; possessive "^a++$" vs "aa" ; atomic "^(?>a)$" vs "a" ; conditional "^(a)?(?(1)b|c)$" vs "ab"=>0 and vs "c"=>0.
- CHARACTER-CLASS EDGE CASES: "[]" and "[^]" are EXCEPTIONS (unterminated character set). "^[]]$" vs "]" => 0 (the first ] after [ or [^ is a literal member) and "^[^]]$" vs "a" => 0. "[[:alpha:]]" is NOT a POSIX class: it is the class [[:alph] followed by a literal ] -> vs "a" => 1, vs "a]" => 0. Bad ranges are exceptions: "[a-\\d]", "[z-a]", "[\\w-a]".
- BRACE QUANTIFIERS: "{,n}" means "{0,n}": "^a{,3}$" vs ""=>0, "aaa"=>0, "aaaa"=>1, "a{,3}"=>1. "{,}" means "{0,}": "^a{,}$" vs ""=>0, "a"=>0, "a{,}"=>1. Unparsable brace forms are LITERAL: "^a{}$" vs "a{}"=>0 / vs "a"=>1; "^a{1,2,3}$" vs "a{1,2,3}"=>0. "a{2,1}" is an exception (min repeat greater than max repeat).
- BACKREFERENCES: "\\1" with no group => exception (invalid group reference 1) even when the instance is ""; "\\8" => exception (invalid group reference 8).
- BAD ESCAPES (exception) are exactly the unknown ASCII-letter escapes: \\z, \\e, \\p (so \\p{L} is fatal), \\k (so \\k<n> is fatal), \\Q, and a trailing lone backslash "a\\" (bad escape (end of pattern)). Escapes of NON-alphanumerics are fine: "^\\-$" vs "-"=>0, "^[\\-]$"=>0, "^[\\/]$" vs "/"=>0, "^a\\\\$" vs a literal backslash => 0. "\\x{61}" => exception (incomplete escape \x).
- LOOKAROUND: lookbehind must be FIXED WIDTH. "(?<=a)b" vs "ab" => 0, but "(?<=a+)b" and "(?<=aa|b)b" => exception (look-behind requires fixed-width pattern). "^(?<=a)b$" vs "ab" => 1 (the ^ pins position 0 so the lookbehind cannot succeed).
- JS-STYLE CONSTRUCTS ARE FATAL: "(?<n>a)" => exception (unknown extension ?<n); "\\k<n>" => exception.
- IGNORECASE (only reachable via (?i)) uses Python's SIMPLE case folding plus a reverse-equivalence table, and is fully Unicode-aware. Confirmed equivalence classes (all => 0): k/K/U+212A KELVIN; s/S/U+017F LONG S; i/I/U+0131 DOTLESS I/U+0130 DOTTED CAPITAL I (all four interchangeable); U+03C3/U+03C2/U+03A3 sigma; U+00E5/U+212B ANGSTROM; U+03C9/U+2126 OHM; U+00B5 MICRO/U+03BC GREEK MU; U+00DF/U+1E9E SHARP S; U+03B9/U+0345 YPOGEGRAMMENI; U+00E9/U+00C9. NOT full casefolding: U+00DF vs "(?i)^ss$" => 1 and "SS" vs "(?i)^ß$" => 1. No compatibility folding: U+FF21 vs "(?i)^a$" => 1. Without (?i): U+212A vs "^k$" => 1, U+00B5 vs "^μ$" => 1.
- IGNORECASE APPLIES INSIDE CLASSES AND RANGES: U+212A vs "(?i)^[k]$" => 0; U+212A, U+017F, U+0131, U+0130 all vs "(?i)^[a-z]$" => 0; the negated form excludes them: U+212A vs "(?i)^[^a-z]$" => 1.
- patternProperties KEY MATCHING IS re.search (unanchored) with all the same Python semantics: {"xay":1} vs patternProperties {"a":{type:string}} => 1, vs {"^a":...} => 0; empty pattern "" and "^$" both match key "" => 1 each; key "a\nb" vs "^b$" => 0 but vs "(?m)^b$" => 1; key "a\n" vs "a$" => 1 (trailing-newline quirk); key "٣" vs "\\d" => 1.
- patternProperties ERROR COUNT = (number of (pattern, key) pairs where re.search hits AND the subschema fails), each independent: 2 patterns matching 1 key => 2 ({"xa":1} vs {"a":str,"^x":str} => 2; {"a":1} vs {"a":str,"^a$":bool} => 2); 1 pattern matching 2 keys => 2 ({"a":1,"b":2} vs {".":str} => 2; {"a":1,"aa":2} vs {"a":str} => 2); multiple regex hits within ONE key still count once ({"aa":1} vs {"a":str} => 1). Nested subschema errors collapse into 1 top-level error ({"a":{"b":1}} vs patternProperties.a.patternProperties.b.type=string => 1).
- patternProperties REGEXES ARE COMPILED PER PROPERTY, so an invalid one is only fatal if the instance is an object with at least one key: {} vs {"patternProperties":{"[":{}}} => 0, 5 => 0, but {"x":1} => exception. An earlier matching valid pattern does not shield a later invalid one: {"x":1} vs {"^x":{type:string},"[":{}} => exception.
- additionalProperties EXCLUSION USES THE SAME re.search: {"ab":1,"b":2} vs {patternProperties:{"^a":{}},additionalProperties:false} => 1 (only "b"); {"xa":1} vs {patternProperties:{"a":{}},additionalProperties:false} => 0 (unanchored hit consumes the key); with additionalProperties as a schema {type:string} the count is also 1.
- properties AND patternProperties BOTH RUN INDEPENDENTLY: {"a":true} vs {properties:{a:{type:string}}, patternProperties:{"^a":{type:number}}} => 2.
- TOP-LEVEL COUNTING AROUND pattern: pattern contributes exactly one error and sums with sibling keywords: {"pattern":"^a$","minLength":5} vs "X" => 2; {"pattern":"^b$","maxLength":2,"enum":["q"]} vs "aaa" => 3. Applicators: allOf yields one top-level error per failing branch ({allOf:[{pattern:"^x"},{pattern:"y$"}]} vs "abc" => 2), while anyOf, oneOf and not each collapse to 1 ({anyOf:[...]} => 1, {oneOf:[{pattern:"^a"},{pattern:"c$"}]} with both matching => 1, {not:{pattern:"b"}} vs "abc" => 1).
- pattern ALSO REACHABLE VIA propertyNames AND items with the same 1-error-per-application rule: {"1":1} vs {propertyNames:{pattern:"^[a-z]+$"}} => 1; ["ab"] vs {items:{pattern:"^b"}} => 1. Their regexes are likewise lazily compiled: [] vs {items:{pattern:"["}} => 0, {} vs {propertyNames:{pattern:"["}} => 0, but {"a":1} vs {propertyNames:{pattern:"["}} => exception.
- re.error PROPAGATES OUT OF EVERYTHING - it is not caught and converted to a validation error: {"type":"number","pattern":"["} vs "abc" => exception (the failing type keyword does not prevent it); {"anyOf":[{"pattern":"["}]} vs "abc" => exception. Exit code is 1 with EMPTY stdout in all such cases.
- DUPLICATE JSON KEYS: last occurrence wins, in both schema and instance (Python json.loads and JS JSON.parse agree). {"patternProperties":{"a":{type:string},"a":{type:number}}} vs {"a":"x"} => 1; {"x":1,"x":"s"} vs {patternProperties:{"x":{type:string}}} => 0.
- OBSERVED DISTRIBUTION over the 221-case corpus: 108 cases print "0\n", 63 print "1\n", 7 print "2\n", 1 prints "3\n", and 42 exit 1 with empty stdout.
GOTCHAS:
- `$` / `^$` and a single trailing newline: Python's `$` matches before ONE trailing \n, JS `$` does not. "a\n" vs {"pattern":"a$"} => 0 and vs "^a$" => 0 and "\n" vs "^$" => 0, while JS /a$/.test("a\n") is false. Fix: translate a trailing unanchored `$` to `(?=\n?$)` semantics, or post-check. Note "a\n\n" => 1 and "a\r" => 1, so only exactly one \n is tolerated. The quirk also applies to patternProperties keys: key "a\n" vs pattern "a$" => 1 (it MATCHED).
- `.` in Python excludes ONLY \n; JS `.` also excludes \r,  ,  . "^a.b$" gives 0 for "a\rb", "a b", "a b" here but JS would give 1. Fix: compile `.` as `[^\n]` (or use the `s` flag plus an explicit \n exclusion).
- `(?m)` in Python splits lines on \n ONLY; JS `m` also breaks at \r,  ,  . "(?m)^b$" => 0 for "a\nb" but 1 for "a\rb", "a b", "a b"; JS with /m would return 0 for all three.
- `\d` is Unicode Nd in Python, ASCII-only in JS. "٣" and "１" and "༠" vs "^\\d$" => 0 (JS: 1). `\D` inverts accordingly: "٣" vs "^\\D$" => 1 (JS: 0). Fix: expand \d to a Nd code-point set (or \p{Nd} with the u flag).
- `\w` is Unicode in Python, [A-Za-z0-9_] in JS. "é", "٣", "²", "½", "Ⅰ", "µ", "中", "ʰ" all give 0 against "^\\w$" (JS: 1). But combining marks are NOT \w: "́" => 1 and "é" vs "^\\w+$" => 1.
- `\b`/`\B` inherit the Unicode \w definition. "éx" vs "\\bx" => 1 (no boundary, because e-acute is a word char) and vs "\\Bx" => 0. Naive JS gives exactly the opposite (0 and 1).
- `\s` set differs at both ends: Python matches U+001C..U+001F and U+0085 (all => 0 vs "^\\s$") which JS \s does not; JS \s matches U+FEFF which Python does NOT ("﻿" vs "^\\s$" => 1, vs "^\\S$" => 0). U+001B is in neither (=> 1).
- Python strings are code-point sequences; JS strings are UTF-16. "😀" vs "^.$" => 0 and vs "^..$" => 1 (naive JS: 1 and 0); "a😀b" vs "^a.b$" => 0. Fix: use the `u`/`v` flag (which also changes escape legality) or iterate code points. Lone surrogates must still work: "\ud800" vs "^.$" => 0 (the `u` flag keeps this working, but beware JSON round-tripping).
- `\Z` and `\A` are real anchors in Python but plain identity escapes ('Z','A') in non-unicode JS. "a" vs "a\\Z" => 0 and "aZ" vs "a\\Z" => 1 (JS: 1 and 0); "a" vs "\\Aa" => 0 and "Aa" vs "\\Aa" => 1 (JS: 1 and 0). Conversely `\z` is a Python re.error => EXIT 1, while JS would match a literal 'z'.
- `[]` and `[^]` are Python re.error (unterminated character set) => EXIT 1; in JS `[]` never matches and `[^]` matches anything. And `[]]`/`[^]]` mean the opposite thing: "]" vs "^[]]$" => 0 and "a" vs "^[^]]$" => 0, whereas JS reads them as empty-class-plus-literal-] / any-plus-literal-] and would give 1 and 1.
- `{,n}` is a real quantifier in Python and literal text in JS. "" vs "^a{,3}$" => 0, "aaaa" => 1, and the literal string "a{,3}" => 1. Same for "{,}" (= {0,}): "a" vs "^a{,}$" => 0, "a{,}" => 1. But "a{}" and "a{1,2,3}" ARE literal in both ("a{}" vs "^a{}$" => 0, "a" => 1).
- `\1` with no capture group is a fatal Python error (invalid group reference), whereas non-unicode JS silently reads it as the octal escape \x01. "" vs "^\\1$" => EXIT 1, not 0. Also "\\8" => EXIT 1. Meanwhile "\\101" IS an octal escape in Python: "A" vs "^\\101$" => 0 (so don't use the `u` flag, which rejects legacy octals, without translating them).
- Variable-width lookbehind is a fatal Python error but perfectly legal in JS: "(?<=a+)b" and "(?<=aa|b)b" => EXIT 1 (look-behind requires fixed-width pattern), where JS would report 0.
- Python-only syntax that a JS RegExp cannot even parse, all observed to WORK here: (?P<n>...) named group, (?P=n) named backref, (?#comment), (?x) verbose, (?a)/(?u) flags, \N{UNICODE NAME}, possessive `a++`, atomic `(?>a)`, conditional `(?(1)yes|no)`. Each returns 0 on a matching instance, so a JS port must rewrite them, not throw.
- JS-only syntax that is FATAL here: "(?<n>a)" (unknown extension ?<n) and "\\k<n>" (bad escape \k) both EXIT 1. Also "\\p{L}" EXIT 1 (bad escape \p) - so a JS port using the `u` flag must NOT accept \p{...} or \k<...>.
- Global inline flags are only legal at offset 0: "a(?i)b", "^(?i)abc$", "((?i)a)" and "(?i)^a(?-i)b$" all EXIT 1. But scoped (?i:...) / (?-i:...) groups are legal anywhere ("aB" vs "^a(?i:b)$" => 0). A JS port must reject mid-pattern (?flags) rather than emulate it.
- IGNORECASE is Unicode simple-casefold PLUS reverse-mapping, matching NEITHER JS mode. Python: U+212A vs "(?i)^k$" => 0, U+017F vs "(?i)^s$" => 0, U+0131 and U+0130 vs "(?i)^i$" => 0, U+00B5 vs "(?i)^μ$" => 0, U+1E9E vs "(?i)^ß$" => 0, U+0345 vs "(?i)^ι$" => 0, and all of these also work inside ranges ("(?i)^[a-z]$" matches U+212A/U+017F/U+0131/U+0130). Non-unicode JS /i/ canonicalization refuses to fold a non-ASCII char onto an ASCII one, so it misses Kelvin/long-s/dotless-i; JS /iu/ folds Kelvin and long-s but NOT U+0131 or U+0130 onto 'i'. Also Python is NOT full-casefold: U+00DF vs "(?i)^ss$" => 1, and NOT compatibility-folding: U+FF21 vs "(?i)^a$" => 1.
- `[[:alpha:]]` is not a POSIX class in either language, but confirm the exact reading: it is the class [[:alph] followed by a LITERAL ]. "a" => 1, "a]" => 0.
- Invalid-regex exceptions are LAZY, so a JS port must not pre-compile schema regexes at construction time. {"pattern":"["} with instance 5 => 0; {"patternProperties":{"[":{}}} with {} => 0 and with 5 => 0, but with {"x":1} => EXIT 1; {"items":{"pattern":"["}} with [] => 0; {"propertyNames":{"pattern":"["}} with {} => 0 and with {"a":1} => EXIT 1. Also {"pattern":"b","patternProperties":{"[":{}}} with "abc" => 0.
- Non-string `pattern` values throw instead of being ignored: {"pattern":5} and {"pattern":null} => EXIT 1 (TypeError first argument must be string or compiled pattern); {"pattern":["b"]} => EXIT 1 (TypeError unhashable type: list). A JS port that does `new RegExp(5)` would happily match "5" instead.
- patternProperties counting is pattern-x-key cross product, not per key: {"xa":1} vs {"a":{type:string},"^x":{type:string}} => 2 and {"a":1} vs {"a":{type:string},"^a$":{type:boolean}} => 2, but repeated regex hits inside one key still count once ({"aa":1} vs {"a":{type:string}} => 1). Nested failures collapse to one top-level error ({"a":{"b":1}} => 1).
- allOf does NOT collapse (2 failing branches => 2 top-level errors) while anyOf/oneOf/not always collapse to 1 - easy to get wrong when summing pattern failures: "abc" vs {allOf:[{pattern:"^x"},{pattern:"y$"}]} => 2 but vs {anyOf:[same]} => 1.
EXCEPTIONS:
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"a\\z"}'  (re.error: bad escape \z at position 1)
- --a '"é"' --b '{"pattern":"(?L)^\\w$"}'  (bad inline flags: cannot use 'L' flag with a str pattern)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"(?#unterminated"}'  (missing ), unterminated comment)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"^\\N{NO SUCH CHARACTER}$"}'  (undefined character name)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"\\p{L}"}'  (bad escape \p at position 0)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"(?<n>a)"}'  (unknown extension ?<n at position 1)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"\\k<n>"}'  (bad escape \k at position 0)
- --a '"ab"' --b '{"pattern":"a(?i)b"}'  (global flags not at the start of the expression)
- --a '"ABC"' --b '{"pattern":"^(?i)abc$"}'  (global flags not at the start of the expression)
- --a '"A"' --b '{"pattern":"((?i)a)"}'  (global flags not at the start of the expression)
- --a '"aB"' --b '{"pattern":"(?i)^a(?-i)b$"}'  (missing : at position 10)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"(?i"}'  (missing -, : or ) at position 3)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"\\Qa\\E"}'  (bad escape \Q at position 0)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"\\1"}'  (invalid group reference 1)
- --a '""' --b '{"pattern":"^\\1$"}'  (invalid group reference 1)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"\\8"}'  (invalid group reference 8)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"["}'  (unterminated character set)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"[]"}'  (unterminated character set)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"[^]"}'  (unterminated character set)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"("}'  (missing ), unterminated subpattern)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":")"}'  (unbalanced parenthesis)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"*"}'  (nothing to repeat)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"a**"}'  (multiple repeat)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"a{2,1}"}'  (min repeat greater than max repeat)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"(?P<1>x)"}'  (bad character in group name '1')
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"(?P<n>a)(?P<n>b)"}'  (redefinition of group name 'n')
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"a\\"}'  i.e. pattern is a single trailing backslash  (bad escape (end of pattern))
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"[a-\\d]"}'  (bad character range a-\d)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"[z-a]"}'  (bad character range z-a)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"[\\w-a]"}'  (bad character range \w-a)
- --a '"ab"' --b '{"pattern":"(?<=a+)b"}'  (look-behind requires fixed-width pattern)
- --a '"ab"' --b '{"pattern":"(?<=aa|b)b"}'  (look-behind requires fixed-width pattern)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"\\e"}'  (bad escape \e at position 0)
- --a '"a"' --b '{"pattern":"\\x{61}"}'  (incomplete escape \x at position 0)
- --a '"abc"' --b '{"pattern":5}'  (TypeError: first argument must be string or compiled pattern)
- --a '"abc"' --b '{"pattern":null}'  (TypeError: first argument must be string or compiled pattern)
- --a '"abc"' --b '{"pattern":["b"]}'  (TypeError: unhashable type: 'list')
- --a '{"x":1}' --b '{"patternProperties":{"[":{}}}'  (unterminated character set; note {} and 5 instances give 0)
